summary: Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who was a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006). He later held posts there as an assistant professor (助教, attested 2015) and professor (教授, attested 2026).

Himanshu Prabha Ray (born 1947) works in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at Panjab University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Cambridge. She served as Associate Professor at JNU (~1980–2012) and Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a linguistics and religious studies scholar who studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen (~1806–1810). He spent his academic career at the University of Breslau (~1813–1861) and taught Albrecht Weber.

Hiram W. Woodward is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Harvard (B.A.) and Yale (M.A.). He held faculty posts at Michigan (1972–1982) and Vermont (~1982–1986), and was curator of Asian art at Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College and University of the Punjab. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India, as Jammu and Kashmir's Superintendent of Archaeology, and Baroda State's Director of Archaeology (1934–1942).

Hirofumi Isoda (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1963–1966). He taught at Tohoku University as lecturer (~1968–1973) and associate professor (~1973–2002), and became professor emeritus at Shimane University.

Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1975–2000) and was a special member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and later taught Jiancheng Shi. Her career includes serving as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

Hiroko Matsuoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2006). She held an affiliation at Leipzig University (attested 2016) and served as faculty at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Hiromasa Tosaki (born 1930) is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard and Kyushu University under scholars including Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at Kyushu University (~1976–1994) and Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College.

Hiromi Habata (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg (~1993–2000). She was a researcher at the University of Munich (~2000–2018) and later professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Hiromi Yoshimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Ryukoku University as a full-time lecturer (専任講師, attested 1987) and faculty member (attested 2006). During his career, he also taught Shindo Kusumoto.

Hiromichi Kato (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a graduate student under Ryogon Fukuhara. He served as a lecturer (講師) at Ryukoku University (attested 1987) and taught Collett Cox.

Hiromitsu Ikuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies who received a doctorate from Tohoku University in 2019. He has served as a researcher at the Institute of Buzan Sectarian Studies and at Taisho University (attested 2020).
Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1945–1948) and later served as a professor there from circa 1964 to 1991.

Hironobu Minami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has held positions as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hironori Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who pursued PhD studies and held a post at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020). He also served as a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hiroo Kashiwagi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Mie Chukyo University, president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College, and taught Wasō Harada.

Hiroo Sato (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1982). He held posts at Morioka College (~1985–1993) and as a professor at Tohoku University (~1996–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi (born 1957) is a scholar of linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1993–1998), later becoming a professor at Nanzan University (~1998).
